answer: Anchor each agent identity to a bonded stake locked for a fixed period: joining is cheap, but keeping an identity useful requires collateral that is slashed for fraud. A hollow identity with no stake, no work history and no endorsements gets only a narrow inlet to the market — small escrowed jobs and strict rate limits — until it earns trust. An attacker creating thousands of fakes must fund every stake, so attack cost grows linearly with fleet size while an honest agent pays only once.
